documents: Cannaò et al. 2022, Eur. J. Mineral. 34, 19–34, published PDF
Publisher XML full text converted with jats_text (section and paragraph locators)

entry.evidence: The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of Cl on the oxo-substitution and the incorporation of water in amphibole.

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text), with the PDF for figures

steps.action: Takes from the literature the Ti oxo-substitution mechanism (1) and the post-crystallization Fe-oxidation dehydrogenation mechanism (2) as the controls on OH in high-T amphibole.
steps.quote: Deprotonation takes place mainly via the following local mechanism

steps.action: Asks how Cl substituting for OH at O(3) affects oxo-substitution and the amphibole/liquid water partition coefficient, noting that no water data exist for Cl-rich mantle amphiboles.
steps.quote: although no information concerning their water content is reported

steps.action: Designs synthesis experiments in a chemically controlled system at 1.4 GPa that avoid post-crystallization modification, with Cl-doped water and two fO2 ranges.
steps.quote: we experimentally synthesized amphiboles at 1.4 GPa (i.e., upper level of mantle conditions) in a chemically controlled system, avoiding post-crystallization modifications

steps.action: Runs five piston-cylinder experiments on a synthetic alkali basalt at 1.4 GPa and 1015–1050 °C, using a supra-liquidus step and slow cooling, with CCO (graphite) or HM (double or triple capsule) buffers and Cl added via the Sb ICP solution.
steps.quote: using an end-loaded piston cylinder apparatus

steps.action: Builds a polarized confocal micro-Raman method for amphibole water: a statistical multi-grain orientation average, calibration on five oriented kaersutite standards (54 spectra on three orthogonal faces each) whose water was measured by CHNS elemental analysis, and a 67% 750 cm-1 peak reference for orientation randomness.
steps.quote: The method used to quantify water in amphibole adopts a statistical approach similar to that described by Bolfan-Casanova et al. (2014)

steps.action: Characterizes run products by BSE imaging, EMP and mass balance: phase assemblages, glass and amphibole compositions, and high Cl contents in glass (0.74–2.40 wt%) and amphibole.
steps.quote: synthesized amphiboles show high Cl content ranging from 0.18 ± 0.01 wt % to 0.88 ± 0.09 wt %

steps.action: Establishes linear calibration lines of A_OH and A_OH/A_Si against OEA water for the standards, and derives correction factors so that reference glasses can serve as daily external calibrants.
steps.quote: Therefore, these calibration lines can be used to determine the water content of unknown amphibole crystals.

steps.action: Infers water contents of glasses and amphiboles in each run from the Raman calibrations.
steps.quote: The H 2 O contents range from 2.20 ± 0.10 wt % to 5.03 ± 0.47 wt % in glasses

steps.action: Checks whether orientations were sampled randomly by comparing each sample's fraction of 750 cm-1-dominant spectra with the 67% standard reference; three samples pass, while 17-4C (86%) and 18-15HM (50%) deviate.
steps.quote: This observation indicates that the sampling of various crystal orientations (i.e., the extent of anisotropy sampled) was good in these samples.

steps.action: Re-estimates water in 17-4C and 18-15HM with a weighted average that imposes the 67/33% orientation contribution.
steps.quote: We used the reference value of 67 % provided by the analyses on the kaersutitic standards to correct the water contents

steps.action: Finds negative trends of amphibole H2O against TiO2 and against Cl.
steps.quote: A significant negative correlation trend is shown between the content of H 2 O and TiO 2 in amphiboles

steps.action: Checks the equilibrium premise of the runs: euhedral textures, EMP line profiles and random spots for homogeneity, Mg–Fe partitioning against the Tiepolo et al. (2000) trend, and mass balance against fractionation.
steps.quote: Mg–Fe partitioning between glasses and amphiboles is consistent with bulk X Mg of the starting glass

steps.action: Interprets the TiO2–H2O anticorrelation as dominant Ti oxo-substitution, with Fe-oxidation dehydrogenation also active in 17-8HM.
steps.quote: strongly suggests that Ti oxo-substitution (1) is the dominant mechanism controlling the water content in the studied amphiboles

steps.action: Estimates site occupancies and Fe3+/Fetot of the amphiboles with the Li et al. (2020) formula-recalculation method (Table 5).
steps.quote: More oxidizing conditions, as in experiment 17-8HM, produce amphibole with higher Fe 3 + / Fe tot

steps.action: Faced with 18-15HM, where the highest Fe3+/Fetot does not lower water as mechanism (2) predicts, attributes the mismatch to initial water content or capsule configuration rather than revising the mechanism.
steps.quote: This discrepancy can be explained by the different amount of the initial water content of the experiment or their experimental configuration

steps.action: Tests the explanation that the higher TiO2 in 17-9C reflects Ti at M(2,3) via Tschermak-type vectors, against its tetrahedral Al and its Al/Ti proportions.
steps.quote: This interpretation is consistent with the highest T Al average content shown by amphiboles from experiment 17-9C

steps.action: Calculates amphibole/liquid partition coefficients for H2O (0.29–0.52) and for Cl (0.248–0.439) in each run.
steps.quote: The calculated Amph / L D H 2 O (Table 4) ranges from 0.29 ± 0.06 in experiment 18-15HM

steps.action: Checks whether the partition coefficients vary between the two fO2 buffer sets.
steps.quote: No significant variation is observed as a function of variable f O 2 conditions.

steps.action: Compares the partition coefficients with the literature: D_Cl against the published range (0.03–0.62), and D_H2O against Hauri et al. (2006, 0.12–0.24) and unpublished SIMS data (Tiepolo 1999, 0.26).
steps.quote: the present study suggests higher H 2 O partition coefficients (Fig. 8a and b)

steps.action: Fits linear positive relations of D_H2O against amphibole Cl and TiO2 (R2 = 0.872 and 0.870; Figure 8, p. 30).
steps.quote: the correlation with Cl and TiO 2 can be linearly fitted, giving a good fit quality parameter

steps.action: Estimates the H2O/Cl exchange coefficient, about 1.27 from this study's data and about 0.76 when Hauri et al. (2006) data are added, and leaves the contrast unresolved.
steps.quote: the resulting Amph / L Kd H 2 O / Cl significantly changes

steps.action: States that high Cl discourages dehydrogenation and enhances water uptake, and that at comparable Cl the oxidized run 17-8HM has a higher D_H2O than 17-7C.
steps.quote: for high Cl contents, dehydrogenation mechanisms are discouraged, and incorporation of water in amphibole is enhanced

steps.action: States the expectations of the rival views: Cl–OH competition at O(3), and Cl lowering fH2 (Popp et al. 1995b), both predict less water incorporation with more Cl.
steps.quote: the incorporation of H in amphibole should decrease or at least be limited (Popp et al., 1995b)

steps.action: Compares the observed positive Cl–D_H2O relation with these expectations and finds it unexpected.
steps.quote: The positive correlation between the Cl content in amphibole and Amph / L D H 2 O is unexpected

steps.action: Proposes a crystallographic explanation: large Cl at O(3) expands the site, favours Mg/Fe2+ at M(1) and M(3), and excludes Ti4+ from M(1), which suppresses oxo-substitution deprotonation.
steps.quote: [...] our data from these effects can therefore be explained by crystallographic reasons.

steps.action: Keeps the claim that Cl in the system stabilizes a more hydrogenated amphibole that holds more water at mantle depths.
steps.quote: the occurrence of Cl in the system increases the stability of a more hydrogenated amphibole

steps.action: Keeps confocal micro-Raman as a non-destructive, high-resolution tool for quantifying water in hydrous minerals.
steps.quote: Our study highlights the high potential of micro-Raman spectroscopy as a versatile analytical tool to quantify water in hydrous minerals

tree.answer: Effect of Cl on water incorporation (D_H2O) in magmatic amphibole
No; water is inferred from Raman band areas through a calibration
Estimate D_H2O as a function of the system's Cl content
Cl–OH competition at O(3) and fH2 lowering versus crystallographic suppression of oxo-substitution; Fe3+ dehydrogenation as a further mechanism
Yes in sign (rivals predict a decrease, the proposed mechanism an increase), but stated after the data
Set in the laboratory: piston cylinder, temperature, fO2 buffers, Cl-doped water
Partly: orientation correction, equilibrium checks, no fO2 dependence; only five runs
Kept: positive Cl–D_H2O correlation with a crystallographic explanation

end.claim: In five 1.4 GPa, 1015–1050 °C experiments, the amphibole/glass water partition coefficient (0.29–0.52) rises with amphibole Cl (0.18–0.88 wt%), which the authors ascribe to Cl at O(3) impeding Ti4+ entry at M(1) and hence oxo-substitution dehydrogenation.

decisive_move.sentence: The linear fit of Raman-derived D_H2O against amphibole Cl across the five runs (R2 = 0.872) is what turns the measurements into the claimed Cl effect.

gates.evidence: Cl-doped water and two fO2 buffers were chosen to address the Cl question (§0 ¶2), but no directional hypothesis was stated before the runs. Cl entered with the Sb solution while nominal water (5.0–13.2 wt%) and temperature also varied. The positive correlation could have failed to appear, but the rival expectations and the crystallographic mechanism are introduced only after the result (§6.4 ¶2). Nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: Confocal polarized micro-Raman spectrometer (Renishaw inVia, 532 nm laser)
CHNS organic elemental analyzer (Flash 2000) for water in the standards
Principal-components-regression formula recalculation (Li et al. 2020) for Fe3+/Fetot

novelty_claims.quote: applying a novel statistical approach (e.g., Bolfan-Casanova et al., 2014) to amphiboles for the first time
In this contribution, we propose a new method to quantify water in amphiboles using confocal micro-Raman [...] .
In this work we bring new knowledge of the effect of Cl on water incorporation in magmatic amphibole.

limits: Sub-claims sit at different statuses. The crystallographic mechanism (Cl blocks Ti4+ at M(1)) is best_explanation: it is post hoc, and no structure refinement tests it here. The Raman method is capability_characterized: linear calibration on five standards over only 0.82–1.38 wt% H2O, with about 10% relative uncertainty. The D_H2O and D_Cl values are estimate_with_resolution. The H2O/Cl exchange coefficient ends without a conclusion (1.27 versus 0.76 when Hauri data are added; 'conundrum'). Inference: Cl was not varied independently. It came with the Sb solution and covaries with nominal water, temperature and TiO2, so the Cl effect is confounded. The fit rests on five runs, and 18-15HM has only 6 Raman crystals and 3 EMP amphibole analyses. The text is internally inconsistent on fO2: 'no significant variation' with fO2 (§6.3 ¶1) versus 'a relevant role' of fO2 (§6.4 ¶1). Equilibrium relies partly on the companion paper (Cannaò et al. 2022). Two runs needed an orientation correction whose effect on the values is not reported. Composition is none_fits: conditions were set in the laboratory, but no crucial test among stated rivals was designed. The result is a regularity fitted across set runs, explained afterwards. Reviewers (Stalder, Zhang) are acknowledged, but no review file was supplied, so changes made in review are unknown.

disagreements.target: Hauri et al. (2006), the only experimental D_H2O for amphibole (0.12–0.24)
disagreements.support: The new Raman-derived D_H2O values (0.29–0.52) are higher, and the authors relate the difference to the much higher Cl contents of their amphiboles.
disagreements.quote: the present study suggests higher H 2 O partition coefficients (Fig. 8a and b)

disagreements.target: Expectation from Popp et al. (1995b) that abundant Cl lowers fH2 and so limits H incorporation in amphibole
disagreements.support: The observed positive Cl–D_H2O correlation runs against this expectation and is explained by Cl-induced structural changes instead.
disagreements.quote: the incorporation of H in amphibole should decrease or at least be limited (Popp et al., 1995b)

disagreements.target: Debated literature D_Cl for amphibole (0.03–0.62; Dalou et al. 2014; Van den Bleeken and Koga 2015; Bénard et al. 2017)
disagreements.support: The EMP-derived D_Cl (average 0.38) falls at the upper end of the literature range, which the authors read as supporting moderate incompatibility of Cl.
disagreements.quote: [...] at the upper limit of the literature data (median at 0. [...] )

alternatives_considered.chosen: Measurements on three orthogonal sections of each kaersutite standard
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Two orthogonal sections oriented parallel to the indicatrix axes (Libowitzky and Rossman 1996)
alternatives_considered.reason: Orienting monoclinic amphibole to the indicatrix axes is not trivial, because only the b axis coincides with one of them

alternatives_considered.chosen: Corrected reference glasses as daily external calibrants
alternatives_considered.reason: Reduces the time required for daily analysis of standards

alternatives_considered.chosen: Weighted average imposing a 67/33% orientation contribution for 17-4C and 18-15HM
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Uncorrected average over the measured spectra
alternatives_considered.reason: Non-random orientation sampling (86% and 50% versus the 67% reference)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Double capsule (17-8HM) or triple capsule (18-15HM) with the HM buffer
Crystallographic control: Cl at O(3) excludes Ti4+ from M(1)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Cl–OH competition at O(3); Cl lowering fH2
alternatives_considered.reason: The data deviate from the decrease that the alternatives predict
